scope: Prospective ITCVE-1@1.4.0 original ToDo UI lifecycle observation only
selection: Retain every serialized controlled-submission receipt in each contiguous phase window. Select exactly one new transaction output with the ToDo PushDrop protocol, nonempty ciphertext and requested two-satoshi amount, independently of the expected verdict. Previously observed transaction IDs cannot be selected again. No candidate or multiple candidates cannot produce a passing lifecycle observation.
faultTarget: For this prospective profile only, a queued baseline verdict is consumed by one new transaction with exactly one matching ToDo protocol/two-satoshi output; previously observed transaction IDs and unrelated background transactions cannot consume it. The public API lifecycle targets its exact pre-derived locking script and two-satoshi amount. Unmatched targets are removed at the phase boundary. Historical unscoped callers retain next-submission behavior.
publicApiBinding: Lifecycle schema3 explicitly opts into this same policy. It retains complete contiguous indexed submission and processAction receipt windows through the public post-call state reads, and selects only the unique new transaction with its exact pre-derived locking script and amount, independently of verdict. The corresponding RPC is selected by the serialized request transaction ID. Child verification independently rederives both selections; native admission joins all submission indices, bytes and verdicts to the global transcript. Schema3 reports without this extension retain their original capture and predicates.
independentBinding: Recompute the exact indexed receipt slice from native-submissions.json; verify serialized bytes, digest, transaction ID, verdict, output index and unique candidate. Independently verify each selected transaction against retained storage bytes and pinned mined ancestry.
historicalPolicy: Historical profiles keep their prior observer. Native attempt42680240116 retains the recorded last-submission false failure and all separate portability and integration failures. Captured diagnostic replay is engineering evidence, not a new native qualification.
